name: Codex
removalRules: Archived and inactive sessions require deletion review. Active sessions and other storage stay protected. Linked Git worktrees retain their review controls.
note: Moppo deletes a session only through `codex delete --force`, after it repeats its checks. Memories, attachments, and generated images stay out of session deletion.
comment: Moppo never edits the Codex databases or decompresses history. The reviewed `CODEX_HOME` goes to the command.

storage.name: Codex task data
storage.comment: Sockets, lock files, markers, temporary folders, the daemon state, shell snapshots, and the companion files of a database or a backup stay with the root. The Git worktree review names each worktree in `worktrees`.

storage.name: Codex sessions
storage.explanation: Saved conversations and task history. Use Codex to manage these files.

storage.name: Codex archived sessions
storage.explanation: Archived conversations can contain task history. Use Codex to manage these files.

storage.name: Codex attachments
storage.explanation: Files attached to tasks. These files can be the only local copies.

storage.name: Codex generated images
storage.explanation: Images created in tasks. These files can be the only local copies.

storage.name: Codex memories
storage.explanation: Persistent memories and supporting files remain protected. Session deletion does not select this folder.

storage.name: Codex plugins
storage.explanation: Installed plugins and their files. Use Codex to manage plugins.

storage.name: Codex other cache files
storage.explanation: The folder name does not prove that removal is safe. Moppo keeps these files protected.

storage.name: Codex temporary files
storage.explanation: These files can belong to active tasks. Moppo keeps them protected.

storage.name: Codex skills
storage.explanation: Installed skills and the bundled system skills. Use Codex to manage skills.
storage.comment: Codex writes its embedded system skills into `skills/.system` at startup and reads user skills from the folder.

storage.name: Codex installed packages
storage.explanation: Codex releases for the background server and the standalone installer. Codex updates and prunes them.
storage.comment: `packages/app-server-daemon` and `packages/standalone` hold `releases`, a `current` link, and the selection history.

storage.name: Codex computer use helper
storage.explanation: The helper application and settings for Computer Use. Use Codex to install or remove the plugin.
storage.comment: The desktop application installs `Codex Computer Use.app` and `config.json` here.

storage.name: Codex recommended skills cache
storage.explanation: A copy of the curated skills repository for recommended skills. Codex refreshes it, so Moppo keeps it protected.
storage.comment: The recommended skills refresh clones `openai/skills` into this folder and keeps `skills-curated-cache.json` beside it.

storage.name: Codex visualizations
storage.explanation: Visualizations created in tasks, in one folder for each conversation. These files can be the only local copies.

storage.name: Codex custom pets
storage.explanation: Custom pet manifests and sprite sheets for the terminal. These files can be the only local copies.
storage.comment: A custom pet is `pets/<name>/pet.json` with its sprite sheet.

storage.name: Codex desktop catalog
storage.explanation: The conversation catalog of the Codex desktop application, with its write-ahead log. Use Codex to manage conversations.
storage.comment: The desktop application keeps `codex.db` here. The command-line databases sit at the top of the folder.

storage.name: Codex settings
storage.explanation: User-level settings, profiles, and feature flags. Use Codex to change them.

storage.name: Codex credentials
storage.explanation: Cached sign-in tokens. Treat this file like a password. Use Codex to sign out.
storage.comment: `auth.lock` beside it serializes writes and stays with the root.

storage.name: Codex message history
storage.explanation: Messages that you typed, one record on each line. Codex trims the file at its size limit.

storage.name: Codex session names
storage.explanation: Names of saved conversations, in an append-only index. Use Codex to rename conversations.
storage.comment: `session_index.jsonl.lock` beside it serializes rewrites and stays with the root.

storage.name: Codex desktop projects
storage.explanation: Projects, their folders, and their conversation lists for the Codex desktop application. Codex keeps a backup beside it.
storage.comment: The desktop application writes this file and `.codex-global-state.json.bak`. The backup stays with the root.

storage.name: Codex state database
storage.explanation: Conversation titles, archive state, projects, and child relationships. Session deletion removes rows only through Codex.
storage.note: Codex names each database with a schema version, such as `state_5.sqlite`, so the name changes when the schema changes.
storage.comment: The `-shm` and `-wal` files beside each database belong to the open database and stay with the root.

storage.name: Codex thread history database
storage.explanation: Paginated conversation history. Codex cannot rebuild this database after a loss.

storage.name: Codex memories database
storage.explanation: Raw memories from earlier conversations and their consolidation progress. Use Codex to delete memories.

storage.name: Codex goals database
storage.explanation: Goals that conversations track and their deferrals. Moppo never edits this database.

storage.name: Codex queue database
storage.explanation: Queued messages that wait for a conversation. Moppo never edits this database.

storage.name: Codex logs database
storage.explanation: Diagnostic logs of the last ten days, within a budget of 64 MiB. Codex prunes them.
